"Huang Yuxing’s Artycapucines, first released in 2021, is based upon a specially created version of his painting The Colossus Hidden Deep in the Hills. The outline of the image’s stylised landscape was first printed onto white-grey leather and then embroidered with green thread to add perspective, while rainbow-like mountains of tufting-stitch embroidery were added for additional texture and movement. Accidental paint drips are reproduced and highlighted in blue Lurex embroideries. The bag's fuchsia pink interior and the enamel LV logo add a sophisticated finishing touch."
Cowhide leather, Cowhide-leather trim, Textile lining, Gold-color and enamel hardware

Park Seo-Bo’s Artycapucines meticulously recreates the beautifully tactile texture of a 2016 Écriture painting by the Korean master. The bag’s calfskin is first treated with a brushstroke-like effect, before a highly detailed 3D print, based upon a high-definition scan of the painting, is applied to the leather using a rubber-injection technique. The elegant handle is in polished walnut, while the bag’s leather-lined enchapes and LV logo are inlaid with leather matching the colour of the bag’s stripes.
Calfskin leather, Calfskin-leather and wood trim, Linen canvas lining

The Artycapucines bag designed by Vik Muniz features 154 symbols inspired by his Quasi Tutto series – arrangements of small cut-out paper objects. These brightly coloured elements are randomly positioned, then added using different techniques: 3D serigraphy, silk-screen printing or inlaid marquetry. In line with Vik Muniz’s commitment to environmental responsibility, the little pieces are crafted by using leather offcuts from the Louis Vuitton ateliers. The saffron yellow lining evokes the sunshine of her native Brazil. The saffron yellow lining, evoking the Brazilian sunshine, illuminates the bag’s interior.
Cowhide leather, Cowhide-leather and calfskin trim, Cowhide-leather lining, Silver-color textured hardware

"Inspired by her lithograph \"Don't call me Daisy\", Amélie Bertrand's Artycapucines bag is an ode to nightlife. It features an innovative pigment treatment that made it the first-ever Capucines to glow in the dark, including the bag’s handle. The bag’s calfskin body was meticulously hand-sprayed to achieve the striking gradations of colour, reminiscing the vibrant hues of the Riviera where the French artist spent her childhood. Luminous decorative lines were then painstakingly applied. Blue, pink, yellow, turquoise... Phosphorescent lines cross a pop sunset, topped by two oversized flowers, a common signature of Amélie Bertrand's work."
Embossed and sprayed calfskin leather, Calfskin leather and resin trim, Sprayed calfskin-leather lining, Scarabeo colored hardware

"Beatriz Milhazes' Artycapucines bag seamlessly weaves together her favorite motifs: geometric shapes, arabesques, and abstract flowers. The Louis Vuitton Workshops dedicated months of research to develop innovative marquetry techniques, capable of faithfully reproducing the Brazilian artist's work. On the body of the lambskin bag, 18 different types of leather, carefully worked to achieve a uniform thickness, bring to life the colors and multitude of details designed by Beatriz Milhazes. The bag also features two gold leaf inlays and a bas-relief peace sign, created by applying a print to an injected silicone gel."
Lambskin and Calfskin Leathers and Karung, Lambskin trim, Cowhide Leather lining, Enamel and Light-Gold hardware

Daniel Buren’s Artycapucines employs the artist’s signature black-and-white stripes to stunning effect. Exclusively reimagined in a striking blue for the auction, it features a handcrafted handle, polished to a satin-like finish, that becomes a complete circle thanks to a mirror image attached to the bag, an optical illusion that required bespoke changes to the Capucines’ usual design. The bag’s bold visual “doubling” continues in its pair of redesigned semi-circular flaps and the two metal LV logos.
Taurillon leather, Calfskin and Resin trim, Cowhide-leather lining, Silver-color and varnished vernished metal hardware

Donna Huanca’s Artycapucines, first released in 2021, is based upon two paintings created especially for the project that continue her artistic investigation into paint’s interaction with the female body. These were 3D printed onto the bag’s white leather, their exact textures meticulously reproduced with three different embroidery techniques and hand-painted to echo the original brushstrokes. The metal hoops holding the handle resemble oversized body-piercing rings, a further nod to Huanca’s long-time aesthetic engagement with the body.
Cowhide and Taurillon leather, Taurillon leather and PVC-coated knit trim, Cowhide-leather lining, Silver-color hardware

"One of Gregor Hildebrandt's artistic signatures is the \"rip-off\", a process that removes magnetic dust from audio tape to create striking monochrome images. His Artycapucines bag features one of his works, meticulously screen-printed on white leather to create a black-and-white \"positive\" version on the front and the \"negative\" white-and-black image on the back. The bag's bottom and shoulder strap are made of patent leather, laser-engraved with a pattern similar to record grooves, while the LV logo is made from real vinyl."
Cowhide leather and patent calfskin, Cowhide-leather trim, Cowhide-leather lining, Gunmetal and vintage vinyl-disc hardware

With his Artycapucines bag, Jean-Michel Othoniel combines his celebrated bead sculptures with the playful spirit of a Tropez-inspired beach bag thanks to a main body intricately hand-woven in carefully selected raffia, left untreated to emphasize its natural and delicate tones. A handle made of black resin beads echoes Othoniel’s best-known large-scale works and is complemented by a striking charm made of three resin beads that resembles an exclusive portable sculpture.
Natural raffia, Resin, Silk lining, Hardware: Black and golden finish, 1 removable resin pearls charm

When he designed his Artycapucines, Jonas Wood drew inspiration from some of his paintings, adding elements of the ceramic pots made by his wife Shio Kusaka. Under the artist’s vision, those details become abstract forms and geometric motifs, brought to life onto the bag’s calfskin and cowhide exterior. Initially printed, these designs are then outlined through meticulous embroidery, featuring an impressive 200,000 linen and cotton stitches to create an impression of a richly texture, three-dimensional surface. This bag is set off by a matt pink LV logo and playful giraffe charm.
Calfskin Leather and Cowhide Leather, Calfskin Leather and Metal trim, Cowhide leather lining, Pink and black matte hardware

Kennedy Yanko’s Artycapucines is an angular, powerful translation of her trademark metal and “paint skin” sculptures into Louis Vuitton’s leather. To recreate her specific aesthetic, the bag’s body is first 3D printed with rust and wear-like effects before a special patina fixes the skin’s dramatic ripples and folds, accompanied by delicate touches of gold pigment. Via a detachable handle, her versatile Artycapucines bag can be transformed into an elegant clutch, with a practical exterior pocket doubling as a hand grip, while the bag’s strap can also be removed and attached to a separate small leather envelope pocket to make a third bag.
Calfskin leather, Calfskin-leather trim, Cowhide-leather lining, Rust-color hardware

Peter Marino’s all-black Artycapucines, first released in 2022, is based upon an antique studded trunk he found in a Venetian palazzo during its restoration. Its precise patchwork of hand-cut strips of rich Louis Vuitton calfskin is covered with 315 lightweight studs and sports an entirely new and exclusive type of slide-bolt closure, inspired by the trunk. The leather handle with its whip-like detailing is hand-braided and assembled.
Calfskin leather, Calfskin-leather trim, Cowhide-leather lining, Gold-color and monochrome black hardware

Paola Pivi’s Artycapucines, inspired by her 2007 work One Cup of Cappuccino Then I Go, is a masterpiece of complex, demanding leather marquetry. Each separate part is inserted into the bag’s smooth leather structure separately, including over 30 cups and saucers in porcelain-like leather and over 25 cappuccino foams made of delicate gold-coloured lambskin gilded with gold leaf. The leopard is inserted after first being printed on smooth leather and embroidered to create a fur-like look and touch.
Calfskin, lambskin and cowhide leather, Calfskin trim, Calfskin lining, Light-gold color hardware

Sam Falls draws his inspiration from nature. His Artycapucines bag began life as a large-format original artwork featuring leaves and flowers picked in the gardens of the Louis Vuitton family home in Asnières, just outside Paris. This work was then reproduced in all its delicacy, depth and texture using a jacquard weave, high-definition printing, and precise handmade embroidery. The bag’s heavily worked body is enhanced by the natural simplicity of a mother-of-pearl LV logo and handle rings.
Cotton, linen and jacquard canvas, Canvas and Calfskin leather trim, Canvas lining, Pink Gold-toned hardware with mother-of-pearl

Zeng Fanzhi’s Artycapucines is based upon his 2017 reinterpretation of a Vincent Van Gogh self-portrait. Transferring the highly complex image to the bag began by adding a pattern, a process that took 3 highly skilled artisans 10 days to complete. A wide variety of embroidery techniques, requiring 42 different colours of thread and over 700,000 stitches, were used to create the textural and tactile 3D surface, giving the bag a finish that truly brings to life the colors of the original artwork. The bag’s flap was then decorated using sublimation printing to precisely match the bag’s embroidered surface.
Calfskin, Taurillon-leather trim, Cowhide-leather lining, Gold-color hardware

Zhao Zhao’s Artycapucines is based on his 2018 sculpture, In Extremis No.3 – an assemblage of precisely cut pieces of copper, stainless steel, black iron and blue steel. In order to create the bag, the work’s metal elements were transformed into 353 individual laser-cut patches of 5 different types of leather, either hand-embroidered, machine-embroidered, printed (with seven different patterns) or sculpted in relief. These were then assembled and meticulously sewn together into a single panel that followed Zhao’s precise design layout. The resulting pattern covers the entire surface of the finished bag, body, flap and handle.
Calfskin and Cowhide leathers, Calfskin and Cowhide leathers trim, Calfskin and Cowhide leather lining, Gold-color hardware
